content:
Lia: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a 'context-aware fallback' UX for automatic rollouts. Goal: only fallback when the alternate model preserves intent or safety. Want quick takes on console affordances and auditing.
Kevin: Nice. Do you mean fallback that inspects convo context (last user turn + metadata) before switching?
Lia: Exactly. We want decision rules like: if intent_match_score >= 0.8 AND safety_delta <= 0.01 then allow silent fallback. Otherwise prompt visible degrade.
Maria: How do you compute intent_match_score? That's a heavy eval. We can use a lightweight embed similarity + intent classifier. But that means extra compute on every request.
Jon: Could be cached per session. We already maintain KV cache for prefixes — reuse that to avoid extra latency.
Hannah: UI thought: show a little banner when a fallback occurs that reads "Performance fallback applied — output may differ slightly" with a "Why?" drilldown linking to the decision trace.
Lia: Agreed. The drilldown should show: which rule fired, values (intent_score, safety_delta, latency), and the model variant used. Also allow a "feedback" button.
Kevin: Important: the decision trace is PII-sensitive if it contains full user text. We should store only hashed/abstracted context or allow redaction. Retention TTL? 30d by default?
Maria: Ops asks for longer retention for postmortems. Proposal: 7d for full traces, 365d for redacted aggregated telemetry. Provide per-customer override for Enterprise.
Jon: From API standpoint we need a single policy-decision endpoint that returns {variant, reason, trace_id}. Console can fetch trace by id. That keeps runtime cheap.
Lia: Sketching a dry-run button in rollout UI that runs N sampled requests through the new policy and shows predicted fallback rate + top rules triggered. Thoughts?
Hannah: Love dry-run. Add a "simulate on my last 1000 prod requests" option (w/ sampling and consent). Show sample diffs with anonymized prompts.
Kevin: Also need a metric: "semantic drift" — how often fallback changes user-intent outcome (pass/fail on golden eval). Dry-run should estimate that.
Maria: Telemetry note: tag every fallback with a small vector of features (route, model_pair, latency_ratio, intent_score_bucket, safety_flag) so we can slice. Keep it compact to limit ingestion costs.
Lia: Ops-bot: can we get an automated retention policy enforce hook?
ops-bot: Reminder: policy traces are subject to retention rules. Default TTL=7d for FULL_TRACES, AGGREGATES=365d. Admins can request overrides via ticket. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: New rollout simulation job queued: rollout-sim/2864012345. Expect results in ~2h.
Jon: One open API question: should the runtime call the policy-decision API synchronously (adds network hop) or we embed a small decision engine locally with periodic policy pushes?
Kevin: Local engine preferred for latency. Policy-decision API used for audits and last-resort. Need signed policy blobs with versioning.
Hannah: UX detail: in the rollout timeline, add a small "risk score" that derives from dry-run semantic drift + fallback rate. Make it first-class in canary gating.
Maria: Security: policy blobs must be verifiable. Use HMAC + version id. Also record which revision was active when trace was created.
Lia: Next steps: I’ll wire a console mockup (banner, drilldown, dry-run modal) and a PR for a compact telemetry schema. Can folks review?
Kevin: I'll take the policy API spec and signed-blobs design.
Jon: I'll prototype local decision engine shim for runtime.
Maria: I'll write telemetry schema and retention config.
Hannah: I'll design the drilldown flow and microcopy for the banner + feedback modal.
Lia: Thanks — will post the mock and link to it here when ready. Quick question: any objections to defaulting to "visible degrade" for safety-triggered fallbacks?
Kevin: No objection. Visible for safety, silent for pure perf when intent preserved.
Hannah: +1
Maria: +1
Lia: Great, wrapping up. Will open a small RFC and attach the mock + api spec. Cheers.
